title: Taking web orders
prompt: What does this program print? The lesson's `orders` table has three web orders: O00007 (227.48), O00008 (59.50) and O00011 (243.00), in that order.
program:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

web = orders.filter(F.col("channel") == "web").select("order_id", "total")
rows = web.take(2)
print(len(rows))
print(rows[0]["order_id"], rows[0]["total"])
print(web.limit(5).count())
hints: `take(2)` is an action that returns a Python list of at most two rows.
`rows[0]` is the first row; `row["name"]` reads one of its values.
`limit(5)` keeps at most five rows. It can't make rows that aren't there.
